content:
iPadOS and macOS were once two very different software platforms. But since iPadOS 26, the two have become increasingly similar. This year, it's even more obvious — iPadOS 27 adds three features that make the iPad more Mac-like than ever.

#1: Status bar displays app name

I use an M5 iPad Pro connected to a Magic Keyboard almost all the time. There's long been a problem with the iPad for keyboard users — the lack of a clear "active app" indicator.

If you only have one app on screen, this isn't a problem. But if you have several apps open at the same time, keyboard shortcuts are easy to press by mistake. I've lost count of how many times I thought a shortcut would trigger in one app, only for it to execute in another.

Mac solved this problem ages ago by showing the name of the active app in the top-left corner of the screen. Now iPadOS 27 can do it too.

iPadOS 27 users will see the name of the active app in the status bar, alongside status bar elements like the time and date. This isn't a huge change, but using the iPad with a keyboard is noticeably more comfortable.

#2: Permanent menu bar

Another welcome change in iPadOS 27 is the ability to set the menu bar to be permanently displayed.

Apple brought the menu bar to the iPad for the first time last year. But unlike on Mac, the menu bar in iPadOS 26 only appeared when the user actively summoned it.

In the Settings app on iPadOS 27, a new option has appeared under "Multitasking & Gestures", labelled "Auto-show and hide menu bar".

Simply turn this option off and the menu bar will stay visible at all times. I've been using it this way during the iPadOS beta period — it's one of my favourite changes this year.

#3: Everyday operations feel more Mac-like in speed

Although I really love my iPad and am grateful for the new features brought by iPadOS 26 and 27, I still get frustrated sometimes by how slow some basic operations are. As I wrote earlier this year: "Right-clicking in iPadOS often feels slow and laggy, but on Mac it's instant."

Fortunately, Apple has been actively fixing this gap this year, and I'm happy to say that iPadOS 27 does show real improvement in the speed of these everyday operations.

Apple says right-click menus open faster when using a cursor, and I can clearly feel it myself. Browsing files and transferring them to an external hard drive is "up to 5x faster" — Apple says that's now as fast as Finder on Mac. App launches are more responsive, and window management is smoother when closing, switching or dragging windows.

There are still areas where Mac is faster, where the iPad feels a bit sluggish. But overall, the speed boost in iPadOS 27 is a big step in the right direction.

Which new features and changes in iPadOS 27 suit you best? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
